narrative.title: Cancelling the nth Reservation from the Back
narrative.scenario: A booking chain lists seats in order, and a cancellation names a seat counted from the rear — awkward on a one-way chain with no length posted. The counter settles it with a two-pointer walk: send one pointer n seats ahead, then advance both until the leader runs out; the follower now stands exactly one seat before the cancellation target.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values and an integer n, the distance from the end of the list.
narrative.outputFormat: The values of the list after removing the n-th node from the end.

testCases.explanation: Counting from the rear, the second seat is 4; relinking skips it.
The only seat is cancelled, leaving an empty chain.

hintLevels: Level 1: From-the-back indexing is the obstacle — the chain only offers from-the-front walking.
Level 2: A fixed gap of n between two walkers converts back-counting into front-walking: when the leader exits, the follower is the target's predecessor.
Level 3: If the leader falls off the end during the head start, the target is the head itself — return the second node; otherwise the follower's next is the node to skip.
